enzyme_name: nucleoside-triphosphate diphosphatase (NTP pyrophosphohydrolase; ITPA/HAM1- or MazG-family)
organism_context: EC 3.6.1.19 is served by unrelated protein families: ITPA/HAM1-type pyrophosphatases (eukaryotes, incl. green algae) and MazG-type NTP pyrophosphohydrolases (bacteria).
rationale: No single protein owns this activity: ITPA/HAM1 enzymes are monofunctional, whereas the Thermotoga maritima MazG protein carries both NTP pyrophosphohydrolase and inorganic pyrophosphatase activities on one chain, and this synthetic '.chlamyexp' entry has no gene assignment to discriminate. IUBMB also deleted EC 3.6.1.19 in 2016 (transferred to EC 3.6.1.9).
direction_note: The equation hydrolyses dGTP but yields AMP (adenine for guanine; the product must be dGMP), yet the only physiological sense of any NTP pyrophosphohydrolase is hydrolytic (left-to-right here) — ModelSEED's '<' would condense AMP + PPi back into a triphosphate.

enzyme_name: aminoacylase-1 (N-acyl-aliphatic-L-amino acid amidohydrolase; 'dehydropeptidase II', acylase I)
organism_context: Mammalian cytosolic ACY1 (human, porcine); homodimeric zinc amidohydrolase. Microbial counterparts (Streptomyces mobaraensis aminoacylase) are likewise single-activity.
rationale: EC 3.5.1.14 is aminoacylase-1/ACY1, a zinc amidohydrolase whose only catalytic activity is hydrolysis of the N-acyl bond of N-acyl-L-amino acids; its synthetic N-acylation under non-physiological conditions is the same reaction run backwards, not a second activity. No bi- or polyfunctional ACY1 form is reported.
direction_note: The products are combinatorial nonsense (L-serine + 2-oxobutyrate instead of acetate + L-glutamate), but the only enzymatically meaningful sense of an aminoacylase is the one consuming N-acetyl-L-glutamate + H2O, which is the left-to-right direction the LLM council picked.

enzyme_name: aminoacylase-1 (N-acyl-aliphatic-L-amino acid amidohydrolase; 'dehydropeptidase II', acylase I)
organism_context: Mammalian cytosolic ACY1 (human, porcine); homodimeric zinc amidohydrolase.
rationale: Same enzyme as rxn38863: ACY1 carries the single activity of hydrolysing N-acyl-L-amino acids, with no reported second catalytic function. Broad acyl-chain tolerance is substrate promiscuity, not bifunctionality.
direction_note: L-lactate + L-threonine cannot arise from N-acetyl-L-glutamate hydrolysis, but the hydrolytic (left-to-right) sense is the only one any aminoacylase runs.

enzyme_name: aminoacylase-1 (N-acyl-aliphatic-L-amino acid amidohydrolase; 'dehydropeptidase II', acylase I)
organism_context: Mammalian cytosolic ACY1 (human, porcine); homodimeric zinc amidohydrolase.
rationale: Same enzyme as rxn38863/rxn38865; ACY1 is a single-activity N-acyl-L-amino acid amidohydrolase. Nothing in the literature supports a fused second catalytic domain.
direction_note: Pyruvate + L-threonine are not hydrolysis products of N-acetyl-L-glutamate, but the N-acyl-amino-acid-consuming (left-to-right) sense is the enzymatically correct one.

organism_context: Human/mammalian cytosolic dCK of the deoxyribonucleoside kinase family.
rationale: dCK is a single-activity NTP:deoxycytidine 5'-phosphotransferase; its very broad donor range (all natural NTPs except dCTP) and acceptor range (dC, dA, dG, araC, gemcitabine) is promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity. No fused second domain is reported for DCK.
direction_note: dGTP is a legitimate donor for dCK but the co-product must be dGDP, not ADP; even so, NTP-driven deoxynucleoside phosphorylation is irreversible in vivo, so the left-to-right (kinase) sense is right and ModelSEED's '<' would have dCMP phosphorylate ADP.

enzyme_name: L-lactate dehydrogenase, FMN-dependent (LldD; yeast flavocytochrome b2/CYB2)
organism_context: Bacterial LldD (quinone-linked, membrane-associated) and S. cerevisiae flavocytochrome b2; the latter's cytochrome b5 haem domain is an electron-transfer module, not a second catalytic activity.
rationale: The MetaCyc template (L-LACTDEHYDROGFMN-RXN) is the FMN-dependent L-lactate dehydrogenase, whose single activity is the two-electron oxidation of L-lactate to pyruvate; the fused haem domain of flavocytochrome b2 only relays electrons to cytochrome c. Multi-subunit Lld complexes are separate polypeptides, which the protocol excludes from bifunctionality.
direction_note: beta-Tocopherol and 2,3-dimethyl-5-phytylquinol are both C28H48O2 cyclisation isomers, not a redox couple, so the two electrons from lactate oxidation go nowhere (charge is off by 2) and the real quinone/cytochrome acceptor that makes this reaction irreversible is absent; lactate-to-pyruvate oxidation is nonetheless the enzyme's only physiological sense.

organism_context: KEGG notes EC 3.6.1.15 occurs in eukaryotes and thermophilic bacteria; the plant (Pisum sativum) enzyme is calmodulin-regulated. Candidates include apyrase/NTPDase-family proteins.
rationale: EC 3.6.1.15 is an unspecific catch-all class (it also hydrolyses NDPs, thiamine diphosphate and FAD) with no single assigned protein, and this synthetic '.chlamyexp' entry carries no gene association, so the catalysing polypeptide cannot be identified. Calling it monofunctional would be a guess rather than a finding.
direction_note: The equation hydrolyses dGTP to ADP + Pi (the product must be dGDP), but every phosphoanhydride hydrolase runs irreversibly in the hydrolytic (left-to-right) sense; ModelSEED's '<' would synthesise a triphosphate from ADP + Pi without an energy source.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana chloroplast phytol-salvage pathway; VTE5 (phytol kinase) makes phytyl-P, VTE6 phosphorylates it to phytyl-PP. These are two separate genes, not a fused enzyme.
rationale: MetaCyc RXN-7763 is the phytyl-phosphate kinase step, assigned to VTE6, a single-activity CTP/NTP-dependent kinase; the preceding phytol kinase step is a different protein (VTE5, with FOLK as a partially redundant paralogue). No bifunctional phytol/phytyl-P kinase is reported.
direction_note: dGTP as donor should give dGDP, not ADP; nevertheless the kinase (left-to-right) sense is the only physiological one, since phytyl-PP is committed to tocopherol/phylloquinone prenylation.

organism_context: KEGG R01887 carries only the generic nitrilase ortholog K01501. In plants, NIT1-NIT3 are monofunctional arylacetonitrilases while the NIT4 subfamily handling cyanoamino acids is a genuine bifunctional beta-cyano-L-alanine hydratase/nitrilase.
rationale: The chemistry is unambiguous (nitrile + 2 H2O -> carboxylate + NH3) but nothing in KEGG or the literature fixes which nitrilase subfamily hydrolyses this gamma-aminonitrile, and the cyanoamino-acid context is exactly where the bifunctional NIT4 type operates. Choosing 'monofunctional' would be an unsupported default.
direction_note: Nitrile hydrolysis to the free carboxylate plus ammonia is irreversible — no nitrilase re-forms a C-N triple bond from glutamate and NH3 — so ModelSEED's '<' is untenable.

organism_context: Streptomyces deoxysugar pathways: UrdR (urdamycin, S. fradiae) gives dTDP-D-olivose; OleU/AknQ are the equivalent 4-ketoreductases in oleandomycin/aclarubicin clusters.
rationale: KEGG R06446 gives no EC and only the comment '4-oxoreductase'; the step is run by a single-activity SDR-family sugar 4-ketoreductase (UrdR/OleU), identified from gene-cluster expression rather than purified mechanism, so the enzyme assignment is inferred. The bifunctional aromatase/ketoreductase LanV of the same pathways acts on the angucycline aglycone, not on the dTDP sugar, and is not this enzyme.
direction_note: Two bare H+ stand in for the NAD(P)H hydride (charge is off by 2), so the couple that sets irreversibility is missing; biosynthetic flux nevertheless runs toward the reduced sugar dTDP-D-olivose, i.e. left-to-right.

organism_context: Defined as a hamster/rat hepatic cytosolic activity (Barnes et al.); the human liver counterpart is bile salt sulfotransferase of the cytosolic hydroxysteroid (SULT2) family.
rationale: Cytosolic sulfotransferases are single-domain, single-activity PAPS-dependent transferases, and EC 2.8.2.34 is a positional (7alpha) specificity of that family rather than a distinct architecture. The specific gene has not been cloned, so the protein identity rests on purified liver-cytosol activity.
direction_note: PAPS is a high-energy sulfuryl donor and sulfotransfer is effectively irreversible in vivo, so the sulfate-forming (left-to-right) sense is the only physiological one.

enzyme_name: sterol Delta7-reductase / 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase (DWF5 in plants, DHCR7 in animals)
organism_context: Plant phytosterol pathway (Arabidopsis DWF5, Marchantia polymorpha MpDWF5A); human DHCR7, loss of which causes Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome. KEGG assigns K00213 / EC 1.3.1.21.
rationale: DWF5/DHCR7 is a single-activity NADPH-dependent polytopic membrane reductase of the C7-C8 sterol double bond; no second catalytic activity is reported (the related DHCR24 Delta24-reductase is a separate gene). Delta5-avenasterol is the plant-pathway equivalent of the DHCR7 product.
direction_note: The EC 1.3.1.21 reaction requires NADPH, but both KEGG R07487 and the ModelSEED entry carry only 2 H+ (charge off by 2), stripping the couple that makes the reduction irreversible; sterol biosynthesis nevertheless runs toward the reduced Delta5 sterol, i.e. left-to-right.

organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus staphyloxanthin pathway; CrtM (dehydrosqualene synthase) and CrtP/AldH/CrtQ are separate proteins.
rationale: CrtN is one flavoprotein desaturase with a single catalytic activity; the three successive desaturations collapsed into this entry (KEGG R09719+R09744+R09745) are its own processive chemistry, not separate enzymes, so the entry is not multi-enzyme. EC 1.3.8.2 defines free FAD as the acceptor, so the flavin couple here is the official statement rather than an abstraction.
direction_note: CrtN is a committed biosynthetic desaturase feeding staphyloxanthin; the FAD-reducing (left-to-right) sense is the physiological one and the reverse would require FADH2 to hydrogenate a polyene.

enzyme_name: cobalt-precorrin-7 (C5)-methyltransferase CbiE, fused as the bifunctional CbiET / CobL in many bacteria
distinct_activities: cobalt-precorrin-7 C5-methyltransferase (EC 2.1.1.289; CbiE domain) — the reaction in this entry
cobalt-precorrin-8 (C15)-methyltransferase with decarboxylation of the C12 acetate side chain (EC 2.1.1.196; CbiT domain; aerobic counterpart EC 2.1.1.132)
organism_context: Fused: Pseudomonas denitrificans CobL and the CbiET proteins covered by KEGG ortholog K00595 (which carries EC 2.1.1.132 + 2.1.1.289 + 2.1.1.196). Split: other bacteria/archaea encode a standalone CbiE (K03399) and CbiT, e.g. Methanocaldococcus jannaschii.
rationale: Blanche et al. purified a single P. denitrificans polypeptide, the cobL product, that performs methylation at C-5 AND at C-15 plus decarboxylation of the C-12 acetate side chain, and the IUBMB entry for EC 2.1.1.289 itself states the equivalent aerobic activity sits on 'the bifunctional enzyme EC 2.1.1.132'. The two methylations are on distinct domains (CbiE-like and CbiT-like) of one chain, so this is genuine fusion bifunctionality, lineage-dependent.
direction_note: The two domains run sequential, not opposed, SAM->SAH methylations committed to corrin ring assembly, so the bifunctionality does not license ModelSEED's reverse call; SAM methyl transfer onto a ring carbon is irreversible.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme — the first committed step is levopimaradiene synthase (GbLPS), followed by several cytochrome P450 oxidations
organism_context: Ginkgo biloba terpene trilactone (ginkgolide) pathway.
rationale: KEGG R08402 is flagged 'multi-step reaction' and reads levopimaradiene <=> ginkgolide A; ModelSEED has further mis-mapped the substrate to copalyl diphosphate, so the entry spans a diterpene cyclisation plus multiple P450 oxidations/lactonisations and no single enzyme catalyses it. 'unknown' is the honest functionality call for a lumped sequence.
direction_note: GbLPS is itself a bifunctional class II/class I diterpene synthase whose internal intermediate is exactly the copalyl diphosphate ModelSEED put on the substrate side, and the whole sequence is committed biosynthesis toward ginkgolide A, so the forward sense is right even though the entry is unusable as a single reaction.

organism_context: Catha edulis (khat) phenylpropylamino alkaloid pathway; the same reduction also occurs in mammalian metabolism of cathinone to (-)-norephedrine and (-)-norpseudoephedrine.
rationale: KEGG R08466 carries no EC and no ortholog and is explicitly flagged 'oxidoreduction / incomplete reaction'; the cathinone -> norephedrine reduction is well documented in khat and in mammals but no protein has been purified or cloned for it. Nothing can be said about mono- vs bifunctionality.
direction_note: Metabolic flux in both khat and mammals runs cathinone -> norephedrine (left-to-right here), and the equation also strips the NAD(P)H hydride down to two bare H+, so ModelSEED's reverse call rests on nothing.

organism_context: Micromonospora megalomicea megalomicin cluster (TDP-L-megosamine route, of which dTDP-L-ristosamine is the intermediate); DesV of Streptomyces venezuelae is the structurally characterised paralogue.
rationale: Sugar 3-aminotransferases of the DesV/MegDIV type are single-activity PLP fold-type I transaminases with no second catalytic domain, but the assignment here is inferred from the chemistry and the megosamine gene set rather than confirmed for this exact entry. KEGG R08594 has been withdrawn, so there is no upstream definition to check against.
direction_note: KEGG R08594 now returns 404 and the ModelSEED equation omits the amino donor/acceptor pair entirely (glutamate / 2-oxoglutarate), so no direction can be read off it; deoxysugar biosynthesis does run toward dTDP-L-ristosamine.

organism_context: Micromonospora megalomicea megalomicin cluster; DesVI (S. venezuelae, desosamine) and TylM1 (tylosin, mycaminose) are the characterised paralogues.
rationale: Sugar N,N-dimethyltransferases perform one catalytic activity applied twice (two successive N-methylations of the same amine), which is not bifunctionality; DesVI has been purified, kinetically characterised and crystallised as a single-domain SAM methyltransferase. The assignment to this withdrawn entry is inferred from the chemistry and the megosamine pathway.
direction_note: KEGG R08595 now returns 404 and the ModelSEED equation omits both SAM and both SAH, so the entry cannot support a direction; the real chemistry (SAM-dependent N-methylation toward dTDP-L-megosamine) is irreversible left-to-right.

enzyme_name: botryococcene C-methyltransferase (triterpene methyltransferase TMT-3; also TMT-1/TMT-2)
organism_context: Botryococcus braunii race B (strain BOT22); heterologously expressed in tobacco and yeast.
rationale: The TMTs are single-activity SAM-dependent C-methyltransferases; KEGG flags R10195 as step 1a of the same enzyme's two-methylation overall reaction (R10199), so the 'two steps' are one enzyme acting twice, not two enzymes. Niehaus et al. identified TMT-1/2/3 by direct functional assay.
direction_note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer onto an unactivated alkene is irreversible; the reverse would require SAH to methylate a saturated hydrocarbon, so the left-to-right sense is the only possible one.

enzyme_name: botryococcene C-methyltransferase (triterpene methyltransferase TMT-3; also TMT-1/TMT-2)
organism_context: Botryococcus braunii race B (strain BOT22).
rationale: Same enzyme as rxn40072 — KEGG R10197 is step 2a of EC 2.1.1.263's own overall two-methylation reaction, differing only in which terminal alkene is methylated first. Single SAM-dependent catalytic activity, no second domain reported.
direction_note: As for rxn40072, SAM-dependent C-methylation of a triterpene is irreversible in the methyl-transferring (left-to-right) sense.

organism_context: Gut and environmental anaerobes — Desulfovibrio desulfuricans, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus. CutC is activated in trans by CutD, a separate radical-SAM activase, so the pair is a two-protein system.
rationale: CutC is a single-activity glycyl radical enzyme catalysing C-N bond cleavage of choline to trimethylamine + acetaldehyde; its activating enzyme CutD is a distinct polypeptide, which the protocol excludes from counting as bifunctionality. Structures and mechanism (Klebsiella CutC) confirm one active site, one activity.
direction_note: Glycyl-radical C-N lysis of choline is irreversible in vivo (TMA is excreted and the radical chemistry is not run backwards), so ModelSEED's '<' would require radical re-amination of acetaldehyde by trimethylamine.

enzyme_name: unidentified — KEGG R10406 assigns no EC and no ortholog to the terpendole G / terpendole B link
organism_context: Fungal indole-diterpene alkaloid pathway (Chaunopycnis alba, Tolypocladium inflatum, Penicillium spp.).
rationale: KEGG R10406 carries no EC, no ortholog and no comment, and the characterised terpendole pathway work (Motoyama et al., Chaunopycnis alba) does not describe a G-to-B interconversion, so no catalysing protein can be named. The two compounds also sit on different KEGG branches (G from terpendole E / paspaline B; B from 12-demethyl-11,12-dehydropaspaline).
direction_note: Terpendole G (C28H37NO4) and terpendole B (C27H35NO3) differ by CH2O with no cosubstrate on either side, so the entry is not a single balanced step and neither direction is supported by enzymology.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana, predominantly in developing/mature seed; SABATH carboxyl methyltransferase family.
rationale: Varbanova et al. showed GAMT1 and GAMT2 are SABATH-family SAM-dependent carboxyl methyltransferases with the single activity of methylating the GA C-6 carboxyl (GA9 and GA4 among the preferred substrates). SABATH enzymes are single-domain; no second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: SAM-dependent carboxyl methyl-esterification is irreversible — ester hydrolysis back to free GA is run by separate methylesterases — so the left-to-right sense is the only enzymatic one for this protein.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana seed; SABATH carboxyl methyltransferase family. Same protein pair as rxn40244, acting on GA4 rather than GA9.
rationale: EC 2.1.1.276 is the GA4 activity of the same GAMT1/GAMT2 SABATH methyltransferases characterised by Varbanova et al.; these are single-domain enzymes with one catalytic activity and a range of GA substrates. Substrate breadth across GA4/GA9 is promiscuity, not bifunctionality.
direction_note: As for rxn40244, SAM-dependent methyl-ester formation is irreversible for the methyltransferase; de-esterification is a different enzyme.

enzyme_name: anthranilate O-methyltransferase / anthranilic acid methyltransferase (AAMT1, AAMT2)
organism_context: Zea mays herbivore-induced AAMT1/AAMT2; orthologous one-step methyl anthranilate synthases in grape (Vitis labrusca), sweet orange and strawberry. SABATH carboxyl methyltransferase family.
rationale: Koellner et al. identified maize AAMT1/AAMT2 as SABATH SAM-dependent methyltransferases that methylate anthranilic acid, and the grape/orange/maize enzymes were later shown to carry out the same single one-step methylation. Single-domain, one catalytic activity.
direction_note: SAM-dependent carboxyl methylation of anthranilate is irreversible in the ester-forming (left-to-right) sense; SAH cannot methylate the free acid back.
